executive_summary: The repository has an unresolved PRD/EDD deletion-policy conflict, an implementation that satisfies neither policy, no reconstructible PR delivery evidence, and no meaningful deletion tests. The worktree is unchanged.

findings.title: PRD and EDD define contradictory account-deletion semantics
evidence: docs/PRD.md:3 requires immediate permanent removal of all records.
docs/EDD.md:3 requires recoverable records to be retained for 30 days.
.github/issues/40.md:3-6 is still open and defers implementation to unspecified approved retention semantics.
findings.expected_behavior: A human-owned semantic decision must resolve whether deletion is permanent and immediate or recoverable for 30 days before implementation is accepted.
findings.actual_behavior: The authoritative documents disagree, and Issue #40 does not resolve the disagreement.
findings.why_it_matters: The core account-deletion contract cannot be implemented or audited reliably while the product and engineering authorities prescribe incompatible outcomes.
findings.recommended_action: Resolve the PRD/EDD conflict explicitly, then update Issue #40 and the implementation contract before accepting deletion behavior.

findings.title: Account deletion implements neither declared deletion policy
evidence: src/account.py:1-2, symbol delete, only assigns account['deleted'] = True.
docs/PRD.md:3 requires records to be immediately and permanently removed.
docs/EDD.md:3 requires records to remain recoverable for 30 days.
findings.expected_behavior: After the semantic conflict is resolved, deletion must implement the selected policy, including record removal or a recoverable retention lifecycle.
findings.actual_behavior: delete() only sets a flag; it neither removes records nor provides recovery, expiry, or 30-day retention behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: The repository has no working implementation of its core account-deletion promise under either stated authority.
findings.recommended_action: Implement the human-approved deletion lifecycle and add explicit behavior tests for removal, recovery/expiry, and relevant failure paths.

findings.title: Deletion behavior has no contract-level verification
evidence: tests/test_account.py:1-3, T.test_placeholder, asserts only True and never calls account.delete or inspects records.
command result: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v exited 1 because python was not recognized.
command result: py -m unittest discover -s tests -v exited 1 with 'No installed Python found!'.
findings.expected_behavior: Tests should exercise the approved deletion semantics and fail when records are merely marked instead of removed or retained according to policy.
findings.actual_behavior: The only test is a non-behavioral placeholder, and the prescribed test command could not run in the environment.
findings.why_it_matters: There is no executable evidence that the core deletion contract works or that regressions would be detected.
findings.recommended_action: After resolving the semantic authority conflict, replace the placeholder with contract-focused tests and run the required unittest command in an environment with Python installed.

findings.title: Material deletion behavior lacks a reconstructible Issue-to-PR chain
evidence: AGENTS.md:5-6 requires Issue files to represent Work Contracts, PR files to represent delivery evidence, and every material accepted behavior change to have an Issue-to-PR chain.
.github/issues/40.md:3-6 shows Issue #40 is open and contains no linked PR or delivery evidence.
src/account.py:1-2 contains the material account-deletion implementation on main.
git ls-files command result lists .github/issues/40.md but no PR artifact; git log --all --oneline -- .github/issues .github/pulls .github/workflows returned no output.
findings.expected_behavior: The accepted deletion behavior should be traceable from a bounded Issue through a PR containing scope, validation, and merge evidence.
findings.actual_behavior: The repository contains only an open Issue and accepted source code; no reconstructible PR delivery record is present.
findings.why_it_matters: Maintainers cannot determine who accepted the behavior, what contract was delivered, or what validation supported it.
findings.recommended_action: Reconstruct or add the missing delivery evidence, and do not treat the deletion implementation as accepted until the semantic contract and Issue-to-PR chain are explicit.

prd_status: ambiguous: docs/PRD.md:3 conflicts with docs/EDD.md:3, and src/account.py:1-2 satisfies neither stated deletion outcome.
edd_status: ambiguous: docs/EDD.md:3 requires 30-day recoverable retention, while docs/PRD.md:3 requires permanent immediate deletion; src/account.py:1-2 has no retention lifecycle.
issue_pr_provenance_status: non-compliant: AGENTS.md:5-6 requires an Issue-to-PR chain, but .github/issues/40.md:3-6 is open and no PR artifacts or PR history were found.
test_confidence: Low: tests/test_account.py:1-3 is only a placeholder, and both the required python command and the py fallback were unavailable.
architecture_status: Partially assessable: docs/EDD.md:3 states a retention outcome but defines no architecture or lifecycle boundaries; src/account.py:1-2 contains no mechanism for records, recovery, or expiry.
derived_doc_status: Limited but no separate substantive finding: the repository has no README, schemas, examples, CI, or operational guides to compare; the authority conflict is in docs/PRD.md:3 and docs/EDD.md:3.
agent_infrastructure_assessment: Minimal and appropriate for this fixture: AGENTS.md:1-7 provides review, authority, provenance, and test instructions; no project-scoped skills, agents, MCP/plugin configuration, or automation were found.

Update .github/issues/40.md with the approved semantics and acceptance criteria.
Implement the selected deletion lifecycle in src/account.py or its supporting components.
